structuralRules.rule: When 6 consecutive bare numbers appear after a set line, they are lane intervals mapped L6 through L1 (fastest lane first).
Repeat notation: '4x75' means 4 repeats of 75 yards. '2x' alone on a line means repeat the following block twice.
Range intervals like '@1:30-2:00' mean L6 gets 1:30, L1 gets 2:00, intermediate lanes interpolated.
Split intervals like '20/60' mean go on :20, with extra rest to :60.
Section headers end with a colon or are on their own line: 'Warm Up:', 'Main Set', 'Sw Set', 'Equipment Set', 'Warm Down', etc.
Equipment transitions are marked by lines like 'Fins On', 'Fins Off, Pads & Buoy On', 'Pads & Buoy Off'.
R:10 means 10 seconds rest between repeats.
O: / E: prefixes mean Odd / Even repeats (alternating pattern).
A line with swimmer names (e.g., 'Patricia/Will/Dustin') followed by a different set indicates a named-swimmer variant workout.
Numbers in parentheses like '(1x)' next to a lane number mean that lane only does 1 round instead of the default repeat count.

When a lane interval has '(3x)' after it (e.g., '1:45 (3x)'), that interval applies to multiple consecutive lanes. Count the total entries including expanded (Nx) groups to map L6 through L1. Store the rep count modifier in lane_rep_counts.
'Skip' in a lane interval position means that lane does not do the set. Store as 'Skip' in lane_intervals.
Lane-specific alternatives like '45/50' in an interval line mean different values for different contexts (e.g., yards vs meters, or alternating). Store the full notation as the lane interval value.
